subtype: Feeling anonymous in a large team [Actor]
passage: Wednesday. Our hackathon team has thirty-two people and I have been doing very little. Nobody knows who wrote what in the shared file, and everything goes under "Team 7". I skipped the last two calls and nobody messaged. Sabina, the coordinator, said "great work, everyone" and I felt nothing. It made me think of last term, when I did the whole marine-life slide for a small group. Everyone praised that one, and I stayed up till two. So maybe it is not laziness, more that this feels like shouting into a big hall. Tomorrow I will ask Sabina whether I can take one named part. — Rehana

qa.q: How many people are on the hackathon team?
qa.a: The hackathon team has thirty-two people.

qa.q: Why does Rehana feel nothing when Sabina says "great work, everyone"?
qa.a: Rehana feels anonymous and unseen, as if the effort cannot be traced or would not matter; the praise is for everyone, so it does not reach anyone.

qa.q: What choice does Rehana make at the end of the entry?
qa.a: Rehana decides to ask Sabina for one named part, so the work is visible, as it was when Rehana did the marine-life slide.

qa.q: What might Sabina, as coordinator of thirty-two people, be seeing about Rehana's calls?
qa.a: Sabina may not have noticed the skipped calls among so many people, which shows how easily one person's absence goes unseen in a big team.

grounding: A student in a big group feels their contribution cannot be traced, so effort drops, though the same student works hard when their part is visible.

subtype: Feeling anonymous in a large team [Actor]
passage:
The college fest decoration team had forty people and one power point that kept tripping. Rain dripped through the canteen roof where they worked.
Tenzin tied a few marigold strings, then sat scrolling his phone. Nobody could tell who did what anyway. Irfan, the coordinator, was shouting at twenty people at once.
Late in the evening, Irfan said, “Tenzin, you take the entrance arch. Just you. Your name goes on the credits board.”
Tenzin looked up. Suddenly the arch was his, and everyone would walk under it. He worked till the guard locked the gate, balancing on a ladder in the rain, fixing each flower himself.
The next day, three people stopped to photograph his arch. He pretended not to watch.

qa.q: What did Irfan give Tenzin to decorate?
qa.a: He gave him the entrance arch.

qa.q: How did Tenzin feel once the arch was his?
qa.a: He felt motivated and responsible, and later quietly proud when people photographed it.

qa.q: What does this suggest team coordinators could do?
qa.a: Give people specific visible parts with their names on them, so effort doesn't get lost in a crowd.

qa.q: How might Irfan feel seeing Tenzin work till the gate closed?
qa.a: Irfan was probably surprised and relieved that giving one clear job changed Tenzin's effort so much.

grounding: Shows a student whose effort drops in a huge, chaotic team, but who works hard once his part is visible and named.

subtype: Feeling anonymous in a large team [Actor]
passage:
Sixty students turned up for the NSS beach clean-up at Besant Nagar. Chaitanya picked up a few plastic bottles, then drifted towards the tea stall. Who would notice one person in sixty?
Preeti, the coordinator, noticed. She said nothing that day.
The next Sunday, she split everyone into stations. “Chaitanya, you're in charge of the recycling sort. Your station, your tally.” She wrote his name on the whiteboard next to a blank count.
Chaitanya was there before anyone else. He sorted glass from plastic, counted bags, chased away a dog trying to chew one. At the end his station had the highest tally. He took a photo of the whiteboard.

qa.q: Where was the NSS beach clean-up?
qa.a: It was at Besant Nagar.

qa.q: What was Chaitanya thinking when he drifted to the tea stall?
qa.a: He felt anonymous and unmotivated, thinking nobody would notice one person in sixty.

qa.q: What did Preeti change, and why did it work?
qa.a: She gave Chaitanya his own station with his name and tally on the board, making his effort visible.

qa.q: How might Preeti have felt seeing the highest tally next to his name?
qa.a: She probably felt pleased and a bit amused that one visible job changed his effort so much.

grounding: Shows a student who slacks in a large anonymous team but works hard when his part is named and visible.

subtype: Feeling anonymous in a large team [Actor]
passage:
“Rajni, were you even singing?” Rekha asked as they left the choir practice.
“Sort of. There are thirty of us. Nobody can hear me.”
“Ma'am can.”
“Ma'am can't hear one voice in thirty.” Rajni shrugged. “I was mouthing mostly.”
The next week, Ms Fernandes stopped the song. “Rajni, you'll sing the first line of the second verse alone.”
Rajni went pale. “Me?”
That night Rekha heard her practising through the hostel wall, over and over.
At the concert Rajni's solo line rang out clearly. Afterwards Rekha grinned. “Nobody can hear one voice in thirty, huh?”
Rajni laughed. “Shut up. I was terrified.”

qa.q: How many singers were in the choir?
qa.a: There were thirty.

qa.q: How did Rajni feel when she was given the solo line?
qa.a: She was terrified; she went pale, but it made her practise hard.

qa.q: What does Rajni's change suggest a choir teacher could do?
qa.a: Giving each singer a visible part now and then makes them feel their voice matters, so they don't just mouth along.

qa.q: How might Rekha have felt hearing the practice through the wall?
qa.a: Rekha was probably amused and a bit proud of a friend for taking it so seriously.

grounding: Shows a student who mouths along in a large choir, feeling unnoticed, but practises hard once given a solo line.

subtype: Feeling anonymous in a large team [Actor]
passage:
I'm Simran, and I'm a little embarrassed about how I behaved during fest prep.
There were forty of us on the logistics team. At the big Sunday meetings I stood at the back, nodded and left early. When the coordinator asked for someone to count chairs, I thought, thirty-nine other people can do it. My name wasn't on anything. Honestly, who would notice?
Then Francis split us into pairs and put up a sheet: "Simran and Leela, registration desk, Gate 2."
Suddenly it was mine. I made queue signs at midnight, printed a backup list and got there at seven. When a parent thanked us both by name, I felt ridiculously proud.
Same person, same fest. The only difference was that my part could be seen.

qa.q: How many people were on the logistics team?
qa.a: There were forty of us on the logistics team.

qa.q: How did Simran feel when a parent thanked the pair by name?
qa.a: Simran felt ridiculously proud, because the work was visibly Simran's own.

qa.q: What could a big team learn from Simran's story?
qa.a: Give each person a small, named task that others can see, so no one feels their effort disappears in the crowd.

qa.q: How might Francis see the change in Simran after the pairs sheet?
qa.a: Francis would likely notice Simran go from leaving early to arriving at seven, and feel pleased the pairs idea worked.

grounding: Shows a student whose effort drops in a large, anonymous team but rises once their part is named and visible.
